points.description: States the purpose: both are more efficient broadcasting methods than flooding, minimising duplicate packets in the network.

Explains Reverse Path Forwarding: on receiving a packet from sender S via neighbour N, the node checks its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all neighbours except N only if N is the next hop it would use to reach S (i.e. the packet arrived on the best reverse path).

Explains Reverse Path Broadcast: nodes learn from observed unicast traffic which spanning-tree paths they lie on, and forward broadcast packets only on those tree edges (excluding the incoming link from N).

rubric.notes: Full mark for stating the efficiency purpose and correctly describing both mechanisms: RPF's reverse-path check against the unicast routing table and RPB's restriction to spanning-tree edges learned from unicast traffic. Equivalent wording is acceptable. Partial credit is not used, since each idea is a single point; a missing or wrong mechanism loses its marks.
